answer: Proof-of-sequential-storage resists sybils: an identity must prove it can read back a large dataset in a verifier-chosen ORDER within a deadline, defeating on-the-fly regeneration — the data must genuinely sit on disk, laid out like a vine along a trellis. A farm cannot fake a dawn of fresh reads across many identities from one anchor of shared storage, because the ordered challenge forces real per-identity resident layout. Honest agents answer their one ordered read; a swarm needs genuine distinct storage per head.
